body:
The input-box readiness predicate no longer refuses on any row that merely holds a compiled modal literal; it refuses only on a standing modal.
A standing modal is a row holding a modal literal that is option-shaped (any indent, optional selector glyph, optional numbering, the literal, only spaces after) or that has no input-box row below it; footer literals never count as the box.
So a modal label quoted mid-sentence in a transcript row above the input box no longer refuses a send on an idle, verified session, while a real dialog still refuses with input-not-ready.
The one predicate still serves viola run's pre-send gate, verify's paste guard, the ledger post-condition and the test rig's box read; no signature, refusal word, detail, exit code, hint, log line, config key, dependency or stamp moved.
The fix is proved over the fake agent, recorded trust screens and named SYNTHETIC screens only; no live claude work; CI green 7/7 on the pushed head.

input-validation decision verify-reads-only-signatures: verify's paste guard reads the moved predicate; the reading is still against compiled characters and literals only, now with a positional rule (row shape, rows below).
input-validation decision verify-pty-output-caught: the verify path reading PTY output through the screen predicate now reads the standing-modal rule; bounds and catch unchanged.

threat-model-summary decision verify-screen-read-against-literals: the screen read still compares only against compiled literals but now also weighs a label row's shape and whether the box stands below it.
threat-model-summary decision verify-signature-only: signatures-only reading holds; the new rule keeps and returns no row text, only a boolean.

authentication-authorization decision unverified-cli-gate: run's pre-send gate refusal at once now fires on a standing modal, not on any label; quiet period, maximum wait and the unverified arm unchanged.

indirect, through the readiness predicate: threat-model-summary decisions upstream-text-is-content and security-anti-patterns-never-do-these decision upstream-text-is-never-a-command, since a modal label quoted in upstream transcript text no longer steers the gate into refusing.

indirect, through the readiness predicate: security-anti-patterns-never-do-these decision compiled-classification-sources, since the new option-shape and box-below rule is built only from the compiled selector glyph and compiled modal and box literals.

indirect, through run's gate: threat-model-summary decisions verify-never-answers-dialogs and verify-writes-no-dialog-byte, since a standing dialog still refuses and no byte is typed into it; an option-shaped label with the box below still refuses.

indirect: the send results input-not-ready refusal keeps its word and hint; only the condition that yields it narrowed, so any row naming when input-not-ready is returned reads the standing-modal rule.

body_fields.fact: A compiled modal literal refuses input readiness only when it stands: its row is option-shaped (indent, optional compiled selector glyph, optional numbering, the literal, then only spaces) or no input-box row stands below it; a footer literal never counts as the box; a label quoted mid-row above the box reads ready.

The standing-modal rule decides on compiled characters and literals alone and keeps or returns no row text; the imports dialog's real screen, the trust dialog's selector row and cell attributes stay unmeasured and decide nothing under it.

The session changed the input-box readiness predicate: a modal literal on the screen now refuses a send only when it stands as a dialog, not whenever any row holds it.
A modal stands when its row is option-shaped (any indent, an optional selector glyph, optional numbering, the literal, then only spaces) or when no input-box row stands below it; a footer literal never counts as box below.
A quoted modal label in a transcript row above an idle input box no longer refuses a send with input-not-ready; a standing modal still refuses at once, and the quiet period, GATE_MAX_WAIT, the poisoned and unverified arms are unchanged.
The one predicate still serves the run pre-send gate, verify's paste guard, the ledger box post-condition and the rig's box read; the start-screen read and verify's settle end keep the raw any-row presence by design.
Added unit cases for each option-shape clause and the box-below rule, two gate-tier cases, a synthetic quoting screen helper and one integration send case past a quoted label; no fixture, schema, stamp, ledger row, refusal word, hint or count moved.

body: The decision that the screen is read only for compiled signatures: still true, but the modal refusal now reads a literal's row shape and whether box rows stand below it, not mere presence anywhere.

The decisions that the rendered child screen is never parsed and that tests make no assertions on the child's screen, in both twins of the test scope summary and the anti-patterns list: the rig's box read moved with the predicate.
The decision that discipline is held at every layer, where it names the screen read over compiled literals only.
The decision that the readiness gate is tested by its refusals: the gate now also carries a delivered case, a send that goes past a quoted modal label to exit 0.
The viola send input-not-ready contract item: it now fires on a standing modal (option-shaped, or no box below), not on any row holding a modal literal.
The readiness gate GATE_MAX_WAIT contract item and the quiet period: unchanged, but they rule over the gate whose at-once modal refusal moved.
The decision that passthrough verdicts never parse the rendered screen, and that no assertion goes beyond compiled literals: rules over the signatures component that now reads row shape.
The decision that the vt100 screen feed is panic-safe and its chaos feed-panic check: rules over the screen component changed; re-run green.
The decision on no blanket dialog approval: a standing dialog still refuses the send, every option-shaped form of each modal literal refuses.
The decision that synthetic test inputs carry a canary and fixture text is synthetic: the new quoting screen is synthetic and the delivered send asserts the canary.
The decision that box rows in screen fixtures are recorded as their literals alone: the synthetic quoting screen places the box rule, prompt and first input-box literal as rows below the quote.

The decision that a fake-agent run is not proof of real-CLI behaviour: the mend is proved over the fake agent, recorded trust screens and synthetic screens; the imports dialog's real screen and the trust selector row stay unmeasured.
The decisions on table-driven rstest unit cases, inline unit tests and test function naming: the new option-shape and box-below cases are rstest case tables inline in the component.
The viola send confirmed-send contract items: a send past a quoted label emits send-issued, prompt-submitted with origin driver and send-confirmed, no send-refused.
The decision on local commands confirmed by post-condition only and the ledger probe contract suite: the ledger box post-condition reads the moved predicate; every stamped set stayed green.
